findings.rationale: Migration output is computed from an earlier read, but commit only checks that each target is still a regular file before blindly renaming the prepared bytes over it. An edit made between planning and commit is silently lost; the multi-file rollback machinery does not detect stale inputs.

The command returns nonzero only when evaluation status is exactly signature-invalid. Other approval failures produced by digest, claim-set, generator, or reviewed-artifact drift therefore leave exit status zero, allowing automation to treat a stale approval as passing.

Approval creation independently loads the model, Git binding, spec digest, and fresh rendering without verifying that the spec stayed unchanged. A concurrent edit can produce and sign a record whose spec digest and requirement set describe one snapshot while its target and claim-set digests describe another.

After detecting a completion without a pending request or a duplicate irreversible completion, replay still attempts the completion action. It then marks the key completed, removes it from pending, and records the outcome even when the model rejects the step, corrupting subsequent lifecycle diagnostics and potentially applying a duplicate transition.

Repeated TOML tables are merged and repeated keys silently overwrite earlier values. A duplicate file, depth, or policy entry is therefore accepted with last-entry-wins behavior, so source ordering can select an unintended verification target instead of producing a manifest error.
